newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Short stg volatility up on election day.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Short stg volatility up on election day.

text.p: Implied volatility of short sterling options traded on LIFFE rose on Thursday as Britain went to the polls, options traders said.
Volumes were thin but traders expected action to pick up tomorrow as markets assessed the new political landscape.

"Tomorrow, things are going to go wild," said a trader at British brokerage. "There'll be the reaction to the election, and on top of that, there's a backlog of trades that people have been putting off until the election is out of the way."
June short sterling options volatility rose to about 10.00 percent from around 9.5 percent at the open, traders said.
June short sterling futures were down two basis points at 93.37.
Rumours swirling through the market that next week's meeting of the UK monetary authorities would be postponed if the opposition Labour Party won the election, supported volatility, traders added.
A spokesman for Labour finance spokesman Gordon Brown declined to comment on the rumours.
Meanwhile gilt options' volatility drifted down as the election, combined with a holiday in continental Europe, drained activity from the market, traders said.
Gilt options trade perked up on Wednesday, as calls at bullish strikes attracted interest. But this session, most investors stayed away, ahead of the election result on Friday.

June gilt options volatility started the day around 8.5 to 8.7 percent, but faded back to 8.1 to 8.2 percent by 1400 GMT. June gilt futures suffered a low volume day and were trading up 3/32 at 110-22.
A trader at a French market-maker in London said opinion was divided about whether there would be a slide in volatility, as political uncertainty was removed.
"I'm expecting a relief rally, and vol should come off," he said. "Even though interest rates may rise a quarter of a point, that's seen as supportive and a sign of monetary prudence."
Elsewhere, Bund volatility traded sideways at 5.4 percent.
